entries.title: How Many Earths Can Fit Inside the Sun?
entries.description:
How many Earths can fit inside the Sun? One point three million.

If the Sun were a hollow sphere, you could pack hundreds of thousands of Earth-sized planets inside it. Diameter-wise, you would need to line up 109 Earths side by side just to span the width of the Sun.

entries.title: The Planet Where It Rains Glass Sideways
entries.description:
Which planet rains glass sideways? Exoplanet HD 189733 b.

This deep blue gas giant experiences supersonic winds blowing at 5,400 miles per hour. The atmosphere is packed with silicate particles, which condense into liquid glass rain flying horizontally.

entries.title: Where Is the Coldest Place in the Universe?
entries.description:
Where is the coldest natural place in the universe? The Boomerang Nebula.

Located 5,000 light years away, it has a temperature of just one Kelvin, which is minus 272 degrees Celsius. Rapidly expanding gas cooling creates this deep cosmic refrigerator.

entries.title: How Much Would You Weigh on Other Planets?
entries.description:
How much would you weigh on other planets? It depends on gravity.

If you weigh 70 kilograms on Earth, you would weigh only 26 kilograms on Mars due to its low mass. But step on Jupiter's crushed gas surface, and you would weigh a massive 175 kilograms.

#Science #Gravity #Weight #Mars #Jupiter #Space #Astronomy #Planets #VisualScience

entries.title: Can Sound Travel Through Space?
entries.description:
Can sound travel through space? No.

Unlike light, sound is a mechanical wave that requires a medium like air or water to travel. Since space is a vacuum with no molecules to collide and transmit energy, cosmic explosions are completely silent.

#Science #SoundWave #SpaceVacuum #CosmicSilence #Acoustics #Space #Astronomy #Explosion #VisualScience
